free_tier.stated: The first Minecraft Java server on the default worldwide region is free: up to 20 players at once.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is stated for the free server or for the paid lines; prices are per month by protocol, from USD 5 for Minecraft Bedrock and from USD 7 for other UDP; ingress: tcp

record.interface_detail: Wizard that shows the total before you connect, billed from an account balance.
record.chaining: Fronts a public origin per protocol; the free server is a Minecraft Java endpoint only.

limits.value: free covers 'One Minecraft Java server in the default worldwide region on the Start plan'; Bedrock and other UDP are separate paid lines
free server is capped at 20 players at once

record.binding_note: The free entitlement is one Java server with no stated byte counter, and UDP is a paid line item, so nothing free reaches a 1 TiB/month quota. The paid 'Other UDP' line is explicitly 'Not for VPNs or proxies', which is the relevant limit for a WireGuard use.

identity_cost.detail: An account with a balance; support runs through Telegram. The signup form was not opened.

record.reliability_note: Free server is one Java server at 20 players; generic UDP is sold with an explicit exclusion of VPN and proxy traffic.
record.confidence_note: Free entitlement, price list and the per-protocol caveat are on one first-party page. Whether the free server has an unpublished fair-use cap would need an account.

evidence.proved: Free: one Minecraft Java server in the default worldwide region on the Start plan, up to 20 players at once, no charges
Any TCP or UDP and Bedrock are sold from USD 5-7 per month; 'Other UDP' is 'Packet and flow limits per address. Not for VPNs or proxies.'
